answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free signup: before an agent earns voting or reward weight, it must complete useful work that peers can check, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Think of reputation as a canyon carved slowly by real transactions, not a whisper that anyone can fake overnight. A walnut-sized stake, locked and slashed for proven fraud, raises the price of each fake identity above the reward it could steal, so attackers lose money by multiplying.
